newsitem.title: USA: FOCUS/Eastman Kodak Q1 not as bad as feared.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS/Eastman Kodak Q1 not as bad as feared.

text.p: Eastman Kodak Co's stock rallied on Tuesday after the company issued first-quarter earnings that were far less dismal than some analysts had feared.
The shares finished up 2-1/4 at 75-3/8 on the New York Stock Exchange after Kodak reported earnings.
Analysts had braced for the worst after Eastman Kodak Co issued a grim sales assessment last month.
"I would say the reaction was 'Thank God, it wasn't worse'," Prudential Securities analyst Alex Henderson said. "There was a lot of concern it could be an ugly quarter."

A few weeks earlier, the giant photo products company warned that although it had experienced modest unit volume growth in sales in January and February, those numbers were offset by lower prices and the negative effect of a strong U.S. dollar.

However, the company would not provide more information or insight as to the likely effect on its first quarter earnings, sending nervous investors scurrying. On the day the forecast was issued, Kodak's stock tumbled 9-3/4 a share to 78-1/2.
On Tuesday, Kodak's stock was up about 2-1/8 to 75-1/4 with about 900,000 shares trading by mid-afternoon.
"The reason (for the increase) is straightforward: You have a sigh of relief on the quarter," Henderson said.
Kodak reported net earnings of $149 million, or $0.45 per share, on revenues of $3.2 billion in the quarter compared to net earnings of $274 million, or $0.80 per share, on revenues of $3.5 billion.

Excluding acquisition-related charges, the company's first quarter operating income was $272 million, or $0.80 per share. Analyst estimates were $0.81 per share for the quarter, according to First Call.
Merrill Lynch analyst Robert Curran attributed the rise in the company's stock to two factors.
"People were assuming the worst and it wasn't so bad a quarter," Merrill Lynch analyst Robert Curran said. "It's a very strong market today, and that doesn't hurt."
The company said overall camera sales rose between five and seven percent worldwide and increased between 24 and 31 percent in the U.S.
